meta.title: Coins - the first form of money 硬币起源

blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 2

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14-26, which are based on Reading Passage 2 on the following pages.

Coins - the first form of money

Question 14 (A):

A Few people pay much attention to coins; we take them for granted. Since the advent of paper currency and the abandonment of a monetary system based on intrinsic or actual value, they have been demoted to the status of change: what is left when you have paid for something with 'paper' money. There is even a belief that they will one day be obsolete, as will paper or plastic notes, and money will at last have achieved the pure status of a mathematical formulation, a system of electronic credits and debits.

Question 15 (B):

B In the modern media environment, the sheer number of visual images is overwhelming, but it makes one stop to think that coins are among the most durable of our artefacts, and future archaeologists will scrutinise coins in order to learn about their distant ancestors. This is exactly the way ancient coins have informed us for over four millennia. There are thousands of different coins, each designed to carry meaning as well as value, tiny but rich sources of documentary evidence about events and cultural attitudes, frequently produced with exquisite craftsmanship.

Question 16 (C):

C Coins in Europe date from 2,500 to 2,700 years ago, and seem to have originated in the ancient kingdom of Lydia, in what is now Turkey. Before coins, trade was based on barter: the direct trade of commodities. Barter required the physical presence of both commodities that were being traded. Metal coins were far more portable, and not subject to the same spoilage on long sea journeys as a commodity like grain might be if it became wet. However, they could also be accumulated, and these hoards could be stolen. Coins were therefore a temptation to criminals. The Greeks, however, were the first to realise the full potential of the new invention. They were a trading people of seafarers. Their civilisation, which was composed of dozens of city-states, was highly decentralised. Despite the potential for theft, the Greeks realised that they could benefit enormously from a system that used coins, because it meant that they no longer had to carry goods with them to barter.

Question 17 (D):

D The value of coins was generally based on the intrinsic value of the metal they were made of. At first this was mostly silver, and this meant that the discovery of silver mines on Greek territory actually increased the quantity of money they could produce. Had the Greek mining been on a larger scale, it could have caused problems similar to those faced by the Spanish centuries later, when so much gold from the New World was brought into their economy that it resulted in serious inflation. One advantage of intrinsic value was that coins could be weighed to determine the amount of metal they contained, so that the only thing an issuing state had to guarantee was the purity of the metal to prevent accusations of fraud and cheating, which could cause fighting and unrest. This was quite difficult to do, especially with coins made of gold, until Archimedes realised that different metals have different weight-volume ratios, and that by measuring the amount of displacement when coins were immersed in water, it was possible to establish whether gold was alloyed with silver.

Question 18 (E):

E All ancient coins were made by hand using engraved metal moulds. Many hundreds of coins were made, and as a result the moulds often cracked and new ones had to be engraved. This explains the endless variety encountered in coins with the same designs because the moulds had to be remade repeatedly, by many different artisans. One of the distinctive features of coins, in fact, is that they are the work of anonymous craftsmen, and yet each coin is an intimate reflection of the character of its city of origin. It was the Greeks who realised that coins could have a double function, as a unit of value and as a symbol of the identity of the city that issued them. The Greek view of life was deeply motivated by a spirit of competition, and coins, which circulated around the trading world, were a way of advertising the qualities of each particular city-state.

Question 19 (F):

F Interestingly, Greek coins from the city of Athens, which was the home of the greatest sculptors of the classical period, seem to have been completely disconnected from the high sculptural tradition. The beautiful features of the city's patron, Athena (with her owl on the reverse of the coin), seem to have been repeated virtually unaltered for many years. Perhaps this was because the Athenian currency had grown increasingly to be the international standard and, like the US dollar today, a uniform design implied integrity.

Question 20 (G):

G One side of a coin was always occupied by the head of a divinity, so it was a relatively small step, at around 323 BC, for Greek coins to replace that head with the portrait of the reigning monarch, a tradition that has continued in monarchies to the present day. Republics may have either symbolic heads going back to the older tradition of divinities or the features of a distinguished past head of state. The Romans adopted the Greek practice of coin design and as a result, the features of many great Romans have survived and are known to modern generations, despite the fact that the art of portrait painting was completely lost for more than a millennium following the fall of the Roman Empire.

Questions 14-20

Reading Passage 2 has seven paragraphs, A-G.

Choose the correct heading for each paragraph from the list of headings below.

Drag a heading from this list and drop it onto the correct paragraph's answer box on the left.

List of Headings
i. Training coin makers
ii. A form of regional promotion
iii. More gold than silver in Greece
iv. Calculating what a coin was worth
v. A simpler, more efficient way of trading
vi. Putting a face to famous historical names
vii. An uncertain future
viii. Careless workmanship caused breakages
ix. Unchanging coins signalled trustworthiness
x. Reading the writing on coins
xi. Significant records of past societies

Questions 21 and 22

Choose TWO letters, A-E.

Which TWO of these comments about ancient coins are made by the writer of the text?

Questions 23-26

Complete the summary below.

Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

Greek traders and coins

The ancient Greek 23 was made up of many city-states which were spread over a large area. Many Greeks were seafarers who travelled the seas trading. Before coins, they had to do this through 24 . This meant that, whenever they set out, they had to carry a lot of goods, which could get damaged on the voyages. The Greeks liked coins; they were made of metal, and the weather and sea had little effect on them. The Greeks had a plentiful supply of 25 which they mined themselves, but were able to avoid the problem of 26 which the Spanish encountered much later, after they allowed too much gold from the New World to enter their economy.

items.text:
（1）题目 14：（题干见题目区）
答案：vii（An uncertain future）
定位：正文 Paragraph A
原文：There is even a belief that they will one day be obsolete, as will paper or plastic notes, and money will at last have achieved the pure status of a mathematical formulation, a system of electronic credits and debits.
译文：甚至有人认为，硬币终有一天会与纸币或塑料钞票一样被淘汰，货币最终会成为由电子贷记和借记构成的纯数学体系。

解析：A段从硬币如今被降为“零钱”的地位写到未来可能彻底退出，因此整段主旨是硬币前途未定，最合适的标题是 “An uncertain future”。

（2）题目 15：（题干见题目区）
答案：xi（Significant records of past societies）
定位：正文 Paragraph B
原文：There are thousands of different coins, each designed to carry meaning as well as value, tiny but rich sources of documentary evidence about events and cultural attitudes, frequently produced with exquisite craftsmanship.
译文：成千上万种硬币不仅承载价值，也承载意义；它们虽小，却是记录事件和文化态度的丰富文献证据。

解析：B段强调硬币耐久、能被未来考古学家研究，并保存事件与文化态度，因此它们是过去社会的重要记录。

（3）题目 16：（题干见题目区）
答案：v（A simpler, more efficient way of trading）
定位：正文 Paragraph C
原文：Despite the potential for theft, the Greeks realised that they could benefit enormously from a system that used coins, because it meant that they no longer had to carry goods with them to barter.
译文：尽管硬币可能被盗，希腊人仍认识到硬币体系能带来巨大好处，因为他们不必再携带货物去以物易物。

解析：C段对比以物易物与便于携带、较不易受潮损坏的金属硬币，中心是硬币让贸易更简单高效。

（4）题目 17：（题干见题目区）
答案：iv（Calculating what a coin was worth）
定位：正文 Paragraph D
原文：One advantage of intrinsic value was that coins could be weighed to determine the amount of metal they contained, so that the only thing an issuing state had to guarantee was the purity of the metal
译文：内在价值体系的一项好处是，可以通过称量硬币来确定其中金属的含量，发行国只需保证金属纯度。

解析：D段解释硬币价值来自金属本身，并介绍称重及阿基米德排水法来判断成分，核心是如何确定硬币价值。

（5）题目 18：（题干见题目区）
答案：ii（A form of regional promotion）
定位：正文 Paragraph E
原文：coins, which circulated around the trading world, were a way of advertising the qualities of each particular city-state.
译文：在贸易世界中流通的硬币，是宣传各个城邦自身特质的一种方式。

解析：E段先说硬币体现发行城市的身份，最后明确说它们用于宣传各城邦的特质，所以标题是区域宣传。

（6）题目 19：（题干见题目区）
答案：ix（Unchanging coins signalled trustworthiness）
定位：正文 Paragraph F
原文：Perhaps this was because the Athenian currency had grown increasingly to be the international standard and, like the US dollar today, a uniform design implied integrity.
译文：这或许是因为雅典货币日益成为国际标准；如同今天的美元，统一不变的设计意味着诚信可靠。

解析：F段说明雅典硬币长期几乎不变，并将 uniform design 与 integrity 联系起来，因此不变的设计传达可信度。

（7）题目 20：（题干见题目区）
答案：vi（Putting a face to famous historical names）
定位：正文 Paragraph G
原文：The Romans adopted the Greek practice of coin design and as a result, the features of many great Romans have survived and are known to modern generations
译文：罗马人采用了希腊人的硬币设计做法，因此许多伟大罗马人的面貌得以保存，并为现代世代所知。

解析：G段写硬币上的头像从神祇转为君主或历史人物，并让后世知道伟大罗马人的面貌，正是“让历史名人有了具体面孔”。

items.text:
（1）题目 21：（题干见题目区）
题目翻译：作者在文中对古代硬币提出了以下哪两项评论？
答案：A（There is no record of the names of the coin makers.）
定位：正文 Paragraph E
原文：One of the distinctive features of coins, in fact, is that they are the work of anonymous craftsmen, and yet each coin is an intimate reflection of the character of its city of origin.
译文：事实上，硬币的一个显著特点是它们出自无名工匠之手，但每枚硬币又都细致地反映了其来源城市的特征。

解析：coin makers 对应 craftsmen，anonymous 表明这些工匠的姓名没有留下记录，因此 A 正确。

（2）题目 22：（题干见题目区）
题目翻译：作者在文中对古代硬币提出了以下哪两项评论？
答案：C（Coins with the same design often looked quite different.）
定位：正文 Paragraph E
原文：This explains the endless variety encountered in coins with the same designs because the moulds had to be remade repeatedly, by many different artisans.
译文：这解释了为何采用同一设计的硬币仍呈现无穷差异：模具必须由许多不同工匠反复重制。

解析：原文直接说同一设计的硬币存在 endless variety，原因是模具由不同工匠反复重制，因此同样设计的硬币外观常有差异，C 正确。

items.text:
（1）题目 23：The ancient Greek ________ was made up of many city-states which were spread over a large area. Many Greeks were seafarers who travelled the seas trading. Before coins, they had to do this through ________. This meant that, whenever they set out, they had to carry a lot of goods, which could get damaged on the voyages. The Greeks liked coins; they were made of metal, and the weather and sea had little effect on them. The Greeks had a plentiful supply of ________ which they mined themselves, but were able to avoid the problem of ________ which the Spanish encountered much later, after they allowed too much gold from the New World to enter their economy.
题目翻译：古希腊的什么由分布在广阔地区的众多城邦组成？
答案：civilisation
定位：正文 Paragraph C
原文：Their civilisation, which was composed of dozens of city-states, was highly decentralised.
译文：他们的文明由数十个城邦组成，权力高度分散。

解析：题干 was made up of many city-states 对应原文 was composed of dozens of city-states，中心名词是 civilisation。

（2）题目 24：The ancient Greek ________ was made up of many city-states which were spread over a large area. Many Greeks were seafarers who travelled the seas trading. Before coins, they had to do this through ________. This meant that, whenever they set out, they had to carry a lot of goods, which could get damaged on the voyages. The Greeks liked coins; they were made of metal, and the weather and sea had little effect on them. The Greeks had a plentiful supply of ________ which they mined themselves, but were able to avoid the problem of ________ which the Spanish encountered much later, after they allowed too much gold from the New World to enter their economy.
题目翻译：硬币出现以前，希腊人通过什么方式进行贸易？
答案：barter
定位：正文 Paragraph C
原文：Before coins, trade was based on barter: the direct trade of commodities.
译文：在硬币出现以前，贸易以物易物为基础，也就是商品之间的直接交换。

解析：题干 through ___ 指代此前的 trading；原文明确说 trade was based on barter，因此填 barter。

（3）题目 25：The ancient Greek ________ was made up of many city-states which were spread over a large area. Many Greeks were seafarers who travelled the seas trading. Before coins, they had to do this through ________. This meant that, whenever they set out, they had to carry a lot of goods, which could get damaged on the voyages. The Greeks liked coins; they were made of metal, and the weather and sea had little effect on them. The Greeks had a plentiful supply of ________ which they mined themselves, but were able to avoid the problem of ________ which the Spanish encountered much later, after they allowed too much gold from the New World to enter their economy.
题目翻译：希腊人自行开采并拥有充足供应的是什么？
答案：silver
定位：正文 Paragraph D
原文：At first this was mostly silver, and this meant that the discovery of silver mines on Greek territory actually increased the quantity of money they could produce.
译文：最初硬币主要由白银制成；希腊领土上发现银矿，使他们能生产更多货币。

解析：原文明确提到 Greek territory 上发现 silver mines，所以他们自行开采且供应充足的是 silver。

（4）题目 26：The ancient Greek ________ was made up of many city-states which were spread over a large area. Many Greeks were seafarers who travelled the seas trading. Before coins, they had to do this through ________. This meant that, whenever they set out, they had to carry a lot of goods, which could get damaged on the voyages. The Greeks liked coins; they were made of metal, and the weather and sea had little effect on them. The Greeks had a plentiful supply of ________ which they mined themselves, but were able to avoid the problem of ________ which the Spanish encountered much later, after they allowed too much gold from the New World to enter their economy.
题目翻译：希腊人避免了西班牙后来遭遇的什么问题？
答案：inflation
定位：正文 Paragraph D
原文：when so much gold from the New World was brought into their economy that it resulted in serious inflation.
译文：来自新大陆的大量黄金进入西班牙经济，结果造成了严重通货膨胀。

解析：题干把 after too much gold entered the economy 改写为原因，原文给出的结果是 serious inflation；限词一词，所以填 inflation。

译文：最初硬币主要由白银制成；希腊领土上发现银矿，使他们能生产更多货币。

解析：原文明确提到 Greek territory 上发现 silver mines，所以他们自行开采且供应充足的是 silver。

（4）题目 26：The ancient Greek ________ was made up of many city-states which were spread over a large area. Many Greeks were seafarers who travelled the seas trading. Before coins, they had to do this through ________. This meant that, whenever they set out, they had to carry a lot of goods, which could get damaged on the voyages. The Greeks liked coins; they were made of metal, and the weather and sea had little effect on them. The Greeks had a plentiful supply of ________ which they mined themselves, but were able to avoid the problem of ________ which the Spanish encountered much later, after they allowed too much gold from the New World to enter their economy.
题目翻译：希腊人避免了西班牙后来遭遇的什么问题？
答案：inflation
定位：正文 Paragraph D
原文：when so much gold from the New World was brought into their economy that it resulted in serious inflation.
译文：来自新大陆的大量黄金进入西班牙经济，结果造成了严重通货膨胀。

解析：题干把 after too much gold entered the economy 改写为原因，原文给出的结果是 serious inflation；限词一词，所以填 inflation。
